introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2024. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in this question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One (booklet 0000/0595/3/Grp 1), Group Three (Grp 3) and Group Four (Grp 4); a candidate sits only ONE group. Group One: Task I (word processing, 15 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks), Task III (HTML, 15 marks). Group Three: Task 1 (word processing, 20 marks), Task 2 (spreadsheet, 15 marks), Task 3 (HTML, 15 marks). Group Four: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks), Task III (C or Pascal program, 10 marks). Each group is worth 50 marks.

The working files named in the tasks (pictures, logo, signature) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**Task I (15 marks)**

The text below is to be typed in a word processor. The title is the first line. The numbers 166 to 169 are references that must end up as superscripts; the last three lines before the name of the authors are bulleted.

Social media verification: assessing sources and visual content

Social media has changed journalism practice. Real-time audience engagement has given rise to crowdsourcing content, and even reporting tasks like verification can now be outsourced to the audience$^{166}$. While journalism remains in essence, a discipline of verification$^{167}$, methods of verifying content and sources require constant updating to reflect the impacts of fast-changing digital technologies, online behaviours, and newsgathering practices. For example, during the Arab Spring, the concept of 'open verification' - a process of public, collaborative, real-time verification - began to surface. But this process remains contentious because of the risks associated with misinformation going viral in the course of attempting to verify information step-by-step in a public forum (i.e. a reporter sharing unverified information with a view to crowdsourcing the verification process)$^{168}$.

Today, eyewitness accounts and visual content are amongst the most important and compelling tools a journalist or news publisher can draw on to tell a high impact story. In a breaking news scenario, speed is a critical factor in verifying information from social media$^{169}$.

Journalists must be able to navigate vast amounts of information to get to sources, information and images that matter. The rapid growth in the amount of visual content (photos, videos and GIFs) uploaded to social platforms, is driven by three main factors:

- The proliferation of camera-enabled smart and feature phones around the world
- Increased access to inexpensive (and in some places, free) mobile data
- The rise of global social networks and social messaging platforms on which anyone can publish content and build an audience

By Tom Trewinnard and Fergus Bell

questions.enonce_markdown: a) Launch the word processor in your computer and type the text above. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open the word processor installed on the computer (for example *Microsoft Word*, *LibreOffice Writer* or *WPS Writer*) and start a new blank document. Type the text **exactly as printed**.

- Type the title on the first line, then each paragraph, pressing **Enter** only at the end of a paragraph (never at the end of a line: the program wraps the lines by itself).
- Respect the punctuation and the spelling: the quotation marks of 'open verification', the dashes between spaces, "step-by-step", "(i.e. a reporter ... verification process)", "GIFs", "newsgathering".
- Type the reference numbers (166, 167, 168, 169) as ordinary digits for the moment, directly after the word or bracket they follow: *audience*, *verification*, *process)* and *social media*. They are made superscript in question c.
- Type the three factors as three separate lines, then the line "By Tom Trewinnard and Fergus Bell".
- Read the text again and correct any error (a typing error loses marks, and the automatic correction of the program sometimes changes a word or a capital letter: check it).

Marking idea (6 marks, indicative): word processor launched and a new document opened (1); title and paragraphs typed with few errors (4); the three factors and the authors' line typed (1).

Click **File > Save As** (or press **Ctrl + S** for a new document), choose the candidate's folder, type the file name **Task 1** and click **Save**. Check that the title bar of the window now shows the name *Task 1*.

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) Format the text as follows:

- Use bold and a 20 points sans serif font for the title. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Select the title line "Social media verification: assessing sources and visual content" (click in the margin to the left of the line, or triple-click it).
2. In the font box choose a **sans serif font** such as *Arial*, *Calibri* or *Verdana* (a sans serif font has no small strokes at the ends of the letters, unlike Times New Roman).
3. In the font size box choose **20**.
4. Click the **Bold** button **B** (or press Ctrl + B).

Marking idea (2 marks): sans serif font at 20 points (1); bold (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) Format the text as follows:

- Use full text justification, a 12 points Times New Roman or a similar serif font, and a line spacing of 1.5 for the paragraphs. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Select all the paragraphs of the text (from the first paragraph to the last bulleted line), but **not** the title which has its own format.
2. In the font box choose **Times New Roman** (a serif font) and in the size box **12**.
3. In the paragraph settings click **Justify** (full justification: the text is aligned on both the left and the right margins, **Ctrl + J**).
4. In the paragraph settings (Line spacing) choose **1.5** lines.

Marking idea (2 marks): serif font Times New Roman at 12 points (1); full justification and line spacing 1.5 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) Format the text as follows:

- Format the four superscript numbers (166 - 169) as indicated in the text. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A superscript is a small character written slightly above the line.

1. Select the number **166** (just after *audience*), then click the **Superscript** button x² of the Font group (Word: **Ctrl + Shift + =**; LibreOffice Writer: **Ctrl + Shift + P**).
2. Do the same for **167** (after *verification*), **168** (after *process)*) and **169** (after *social media*).
3. Check that the four numbers are above the line, directly attached to the word, and that nothing else is raised.

Marking idea (2 marks, indicative): at least two numbers correctly raised (1); all four correct (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) Format the text as follows:

- Use bullets to list out the last three lines as shown. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the three lines that follow "...is driven by three main factors:" (The proliferation of camera-enabled ... / Increased access to inexpensive ... / The rise of global social networks ...) and click the **Bullets** button of the Paragraph group. Each of the three lines then starts with a bullet (a round dot) and is indented.

Marking idea (1 mark): bullets applied to the three lines only.

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) Format the text as follows:

- Insert the image UN.jpg before the title of the document. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The picture file **UN.jpg** is supplied on the day (it is not reproduced in the question paper).

1. Place the cursor at the very beginning of the document (**Ctrl + Home**) and press **Enter** to create an empty line above the title; move back to that empty line.
2. Click **Insert > Picture** (Pictures > This Device), look for the file **UN.jpg** in the folder indicated by the invigilator, select it and click **Insert**.
3. If the picture is too big, drag a corner handle to reduce it (keep the proportions) so that it stays above the title and does not push the text onto another page.

Marking idea (2 marks): picture UN.jpg inserted (1); placed before (above) the title (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: d) Save your document as Task 2.
questions.corrige_markdown: Click **File > Save As** and type the new name **Task 2**. Using *Save As* (and not *Save*) keeps the first file **Task 1** unformatted and creates a second file with the formatting.

Click **File > Print**, check the print preview (the picture, the title, the justified paragraphs and the bullets must be visible on the page), choose the printer given by the invigilator, 1 copy, and click **Print**. Write the candidate's name and number on the printed page if asked.
